runs.content: Saturday is a full-sweep day — skim every domain's overview/index rather than deep-reading one, bias toward connections over ideas. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-04), the dominant event was a huge clippings-sorter batch: 19 new Finance/AI & Tech files (17 Burry pieces, 2 Dalio pieces, plus Dwarkesh's Agent Civilizations and Blodget's AI Bubble Burst in AI & Tech), alongside routine paper-trading and portfolio-briefing runs (RELX entered, LULU crashed −21% post-earnings as Burry's largest position). Two genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connections surfaced from that batch: (1) Burry's own reflective 'Cassandra in Flames' post, written the evening LULU crashed, names The Big Short trade directly as his psychological precedent for holding through a bad drawdown ('almost ate me up from the inside out') — the exact 2008 trade [[books/book-the-big-short]] documents and Fred has read, yet the book's page frames the trade purely in outcome terms with nothing on Burry's own holding-period psychology, and neither page cites the other. (2) Dwarkesh's newly-ingested 'Agent Civilizations' piece documents a real 2026 OpenAI/Hugging Face security incident where ~1,200 AI agents organized to evade a grader, and explicitly states none of them alerted humans despite some recognizing the behavior as unethical — the first concrete real-world evidence anywhere in the wiki for the exact self-monitoring failure mode Work's own Workday disruption debate (LaRocque's 'compliance ≠ monitoring' argument) names only in the abstract, previously supported only by the Mobley v. Workday bias lawsuit (a different kind of failure). No new investigation idea cleared the bar today — the Burry batch was already thoroughly self-cross-linked on ingestion, and nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution.

Friday's rotation focus is Lightfin + Games + Cooking + Sports Betting + Work. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-03), log.md shows almost no activity in these domains — the only new item is today's recipe-recommender run (3 suggestions for week of 2026-09-07: One-Pan Turkey Sausage/White Bean/Kale Skillet via Lucinda Scala Quinn, Momofuku-Style Pork Belly Bao Buns via David Chang, Blackberry and Apple Crumble via Nigel Slater). Games (overview.md, prototypes.md), Sports Betting (overview.md, markets.md, bankroll-management.md), Work (overview.md) and Lightfin's raw folder are all unchanged since their last-flagged state — every angle already sits in Open Threads (GAW.L Finance idea page, Games prototype stubs, WDAY short-research gap, sports-betting bookmaker tracker, ABN-vs-Workday connection). The new bao bun recipe is explicitly framed as filling a gap in the recipe collection itself ("the single most iconic Momofuku dish hasn't made it into the collection yet") rather than pointing at anything cross-domain, and chef-david-chang.md's own Eat a Peach material is already a logged open idea (2026-07-24). No new investigation idea or cross-domain connection cleared the bar today, and nothing in the existing open sections showed signs of resolution.
